feature: Timeline rows open into their sub-layers, like the Layers list
summary: Anything on the timeline made of parts (a title page, a name card, a group, a group of groups) now has an arrow. Opened, each part is its own row one step in, with its own bar, so you can pick it, retime it and drag it on its own. Closed, it is one row with faint marks showing where its parts' timings fall.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording with the timeline showing.

try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does a part row one step in under its track read as part of that clip, the way a layer inside a group reads in the Layers list?
Are the faint marks on a closed title's bar enough to tell you there is timing inside to open, without being noise?
Should a part's own moving values (the Opacity row under the Subtitle) be indented under the part too, or is the left margin right?
Is the arrow plus Option-click enough, or do you want a key for opening and closing rows?
rough: Right and Left arrows do not open or close rows: on a video they are Premiere's frame step, and with a layer picked Photoshop's nudge, so opening and closing stays on the arrow and Option-click (UX-PATTERNS §7).

Opening a row is shared with the Layers list (one set of open groups) and is remembered per file the way the list remembers it, in the app's settings rather than inside the document, so opening a row is never an undo step and never marks the file edited.

While the timeline stands in for the Layers list, picking a part on the canvas no longer opens its groups; the timeline shows the picked part's row under a closed one by itself, so a pick never pushes the tracks below out of sight.
A part of a copy of a component is listed with its bar, but the bar does not drag: a copy's contents are rewritten from its original, so the change would be lost on the next sync.
Logos: an SVG or PNG logo lands on the timeline as one picture with no layers, so it has nothing to open. Size measurement groups on a video were not tried in this pass.
A part's moving-value rows (Opacity, Position) keep their labels at the left margin rather than indented under the part.
No mock page draws nested timeline rows; this follows the Layers list, the model you named on 2026-10-17, and the placement contract's Timeline row now says so.
